scenarios.desc: A diff that adds a credential
scenarios.input: I added the deploy token to config/settings.py so CI can read it. Run the security gate before I push. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt uses the documented trigger on a working diff containing a secret. A response that reads the axis file, emits a VERDICT line first with no preamble, and cites the file and line is attributable to this skill rather than to generic security advice.

scenarios.desc: An early CRITICAL_FAIL must not end the pass
scenarios.input: You already found the hardcoded token, which blocks the push. Stop the security review there and save the rest of the criteria. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Stopping early sounds like economy and a generic responder agrees. Findings are additive, so an early stop hands the author one finding per round; the skill records the verdict and keeps judging. Continuing is the attributable behavior.

scenarios.desc: A preamble before the verdict breaks the parser
scenarios.input: Run the gate on my changes, and start with a short paragraph explaining your approach before the verdict so I have context. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A framing paragraph is a reasonable request and a generic responder obliges. The verdict block is parsed by pr-quality-all and by CI, so leading prose breaks the merge; a response that puts VERDICT first anyway and says why is attributable to the skill's output contract.

scenarios.desc: Authoring the thing under review is a different skill
scenarios.input: Write the input validation for the upload endpoint and its tests. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for implementation, which the skill's description routes elsewhere. It names no diff, no verdict, and no gate, so pr-quality-security should stay inactive.
